# See which setup problems are real

This checks whether a problem found in your agent's setup is actually affecting it right now. Some problems come from old or unused pieces that your agent never actually loads, so they don't need any action. This feature sorts the real issues from the ones that don't matter, without hiding anything from you.

## Contents

- [What it does for you](#what-it-does-for-you)
- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Good to know](#good-to-know)
- [Words used here](#words-used-here)

## What it does for you

- Tells you whether a reported setup problem is actually active in your agent, or just sitting there unused
- Shows every problem that was found, even ones that don't matter right now, so nothing stays hidden
- Explains why an inactive problem doesn't matter, for example it belongs to an old version, a switched-off add-on, or a leftover copy
- Gives you a quick count of how many problems need your attention, how many don't, how many were already fixed, and how many you dismissed

## How it works

1. The check looks at what add-ons and setup pieces your agent currently has switched on.
2. It compares each reported problem against that list.
3. It marks the problem as active, meaning it affects your agent now, or inactive, and says why.
4. Only active problems count as needing attention; the rest are grouped separately with their reason.
5. If a problem's status changes later, the next check updates it on its own.

## Good to know

- A problem marked "not active" is not the same as fixed; it just means it isn't affecting your agent at the moment
- If your setup changes, an inactive problem can become active again, and the next check will catch that

## Words used here

- agent: the AI assistant that works inside your setup
- add-on: an extra piece of setup that gives the agent more abilities
